      Read the data well

      Methodology & sources

      01

      Source

      Figures come from the U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-year Detailed Tables API. State boundaries come from Census cartographic data distributed by the open-source us-atlas project.

      02

      Uncertainty

      ACS figures are survey estimates. Published 90% margins of error appear with headline measures when available. Calculated rates do not include margins of error.

      03

      Availability

      ACS 5-year data cover every state and county. If the API is unavailable, the dashboard switches to a clearly labeled demo dataset.

      04

      Privacy

      The dashboard uses no accounts or analytics. A Census API key stays only in page memory and is sent directly to api.census.gov for Census requests.

      05

      Comparability

      Adjacent ACS 5-year estimates share four years of survey responses. For non-overlapping comparisons, compare 2015–2019 with 2020–2024 and check Census variable-change notes.

      About the lab

      Quantitative Histories Workshop

      The Quantitative Histories Workshop is a computational curriculum collective and community-centered teaching and learning lab organized around a network of collaborative projects. We use interdisciplinary perspectives and computational tools to study history, develop open educational resources and software, and explore questions of justice and futurity. As an open community, we invite knowledge exchange among participants who investigate historical events, explore data, and consider how historical understanding can inform action in the present and possibilities for the future.

      Find out more about the workshop ↗
      Your privacy

      Your Census API key is kept only in memory while this page is open. It is never stored by Census Atlas, added to the page’s shareable URL, or included in an export. Census queries send the key directly to the Census Bureau over HTTPS, where requests may be logged. Census Atlas has no accounts or analytics and does not collect the information you enter.

      Use your Census API key

      Your key stays in memory while this page is open and is never stored by Census Atlas. Census requests send it directly to api.census.gov over HTTPS as a query parameter; the Census Bureau may log those requests. It is not added to this page’s shareable URL or exports.
